title: RankCal: Counterfactual Influence Quantization for Action-Conditioned Latent World-Model Planning
abstract_draft: Quantizing an action-conditioned latent world model is difficult because small numerical errors can change which imagined action sequence a planner ranks first, and those ranking changes compound through closed-loop replanning. The bottleneck is not captured by tensor reconstruction alone: An Empirical Study of World Model Quantization (arxiv:2602.02110v1) reports that post-training quantization effects vary by bit-width, granularity, module, and planning horizon, with planning-objective and task-success mismatch. RankCal proposes a site-only counterfactual influence profile: with the planner, candidate pool, rollout convention, and all other sites fixed in FP16, quantize one site at a time and measure its effect on candidate ordering over action-conditioned latent rollouts. It then assigns weight/activation bit pairs by minimizing this influence under a measured `PeakBytes` budget and fixed bit histogram. The falsification prediction is that, at matched memory and nominal bit-width, RankCal improves candidate-order agreement and closed-loop task success over uniform-bit and local-reconstruction allocation, especially at longer horizons; permuting the influence-to-site mapping should remove the benefit. A positive result would turn decision-level sensitivity into a deployable mixed-precision PTQ signal, while a null or permutation-insensitive result would reject the proposed mechanism. The proposal targets imagined action-sequence latent-dynamics planning and does not claim a method for joint video/action denoising in World Action Models.
core_claim: At matched measured `PeakBytes` and nominal bit-width, allocating protection according to site-only rollout-ranking influence preserves candidate order and closed-loop task success in an action-conditioned latent world-model planner better than local reconstruction error, especially at longer horizons.

sub_claims.statement: At matched measured `PeakBytes` and nominal bit-width, the site-only rollout-ranking influence profile predicts which quantizable sites must be protected to preserve candidate order better than local tensor reconstruction error.
sub_claims.supports_which_aspect: Closes the planning-objective/task-success mismatch caused by module- and horizon-dependent PTQ effects.

sub_claims.statement: An assignment optimized from that profile can preserve longer-horizon closed-loop action consequences even when its tensor-MSE allocation is worse.
sub_claims.supports_which_aspect: Closes the gap between local reconstruction quality and downstream success after an altered action propagates through latent dynamics.

sub_claims.statement: If the influence-to-site mapping is permuted while the bit histogram, memory, planner schedule, and tie rules are fixed, the downstream advantage should disappear.
sub_claims.supports_which_aspect: Distinguishes the proposed decision-level signal from generic benefits of mixed precision or simply assigning more bits.

key_equations.description: Roll out each candidate action sequence through the frozen action-conditioned latent dynamics.
key_equations.description_zh: 在冻结的 action-conditioned latent dynamics 中，对每条候选 action sequence 进行 imagined rollout。

key_equations.description: Measure pairwise candidate-order agreement after quantizing only site g with bit pair b, then convert disagreement into influence.
key_equations.description_zh: 只量化 site g 为 bit pair b，比较候选 action sequence 的两两排序一致性，并把不一致度转成 influence。

key_equations.description: Choose the mixed W/A assignment with the smallest aggregate ranking influence under a measured peak-memory budget and fixed bit histogram.
key_equations.description_zh: 在 measured `PeakBytes` 预算和固定 bit histogram 约束下，选择 aggregate ranking influence 最小的 mixed W/A assignment。

method_flow.high_level_pipeline: RankCal takes a frozen FP16 action-conditioned latent world model, planner inputs, candidate action sequences, and quantization site/bit-pair options. It holds the planner and rollout convention fixed, quantizes one site at a time, and measures how each intervention changes the ordering of imagined action sequences over latent dynamics. The resulting site-by-bit influence profile is converted into a mixed W/A assignment by minimizing influence under measured `PeakBytes` and a fixed nominal bit histogram. The output is a quantized checkpoint for the unchanged receding-horizon planner, whose candidate ordering and closed-loop action consequences remain the objects of evaluation; joint video/action denoising in WAMs is outside this branch.

steps.title: Freeze the imagined-rollout probe
steps.what_changes: Fix the FP16 planner inputs, candidate action-sequence pool, receding-horizon convention, tie rule, and latent rollout evaluator; expose one quantizable weight/activation site at a time while all other sites remain FP16.
steps.why_this_step: This isolates a site-level perturbation in the action-conditioned latent-dynamics branch and prevents planner redesign or WAM denoising changes from being mistaken for quantization effects.
steps.input: FP16 action-conditioned latent world model, planner inputs, candidate pool, and quantization site/bit-pair candidates.
steps.output: A reproducible frozen probe that returns FP16 and one-site-quantized rollout scores for the same candidate sequences.

steps.title: Estimate rollout-ranking influence
steps.what_changes: For each site and bit pair, compare the FP16 and one-site-quantized candidate ordering over imagined latent rollouts, retaining horizon-specific influence values I_g(b).
steps.why_this_step: The ranking estimand closes the gap between tensor reconstruction error and the planner's decision-level sensitivity, including the downstream consequence of an altered selected action.
steps.input: Frozen probe outputs from the frozen-probe step.
steps.output: A site-by-bit influence profile I_g(b) indexed by rollout horizon and quantizable site.

steps.title: Allocate bits under measured memory
steps.what_changes: Choose each site's weight/activation bit pair by minimizing aggregate influence subject to measured `PeakBytes` and the fixed nominal bit histogram.
steps.why_this_step: This converts the diagnostic profile into a deployable mixed W/A PTQ assignment without changing the latent planner or replacing measured memory with a nominal byte assumption.
steps.input: Site-by-bit influence profile, candidate bit pairs, backend-specific byte accounting, target bit histogram, and memory budget B.
steps.output: A mixed W/A assignment `b*` and a quantized checkpoint candidate.

steps.title: Preserve closed-loop action consequences
steps.what_changes: Apply the assignment to the frozen planner and run its normal imagined action-sequence and receding-horizon loop, recording candidate-order agreement, first-action agreement, and closed-loop task success under the prescribed horizon conditions. Within this existing all-sites evaluation, treat representative high/low-influence site pairs as a tactical interaction diagnostic: compare measured joint candidate-order discordance with the corresponding single-site values under the same candidate pool, bit histogram, measured `PeakBytes`, memory target, planner schedule, receding-horizon convention, and tie rule; if an exact feasible match cannot be constructed, record the diagnostic as unavailable, and use any discrepancy only to bound the site-wise allocation interpretation without defining a new estimand or claiming joint optimality.
steps.why_this_step: The object to preserve is the selected action and its later consequences, so the evaluation stays in latent-dynamics planning rather than switching to joint video/action denoising. The pair diagnostic tests the interaction boundary inside the same all-sites evaluation without changing the site-only estimand or falsification prediction.
steps.input: Quantized checkpoint candidate and the unchanged planner and evaluation convention from the frozen-probe step.
steps.output: Closed-loop rollout outcomes and decision-level diagnostics for assessing whether RankCal's allocation signal is load-bearing.

method_flow.design_reasoning_echo: RankCal chooses the decision-level object because the failure of interest is an ordering change that propagates through receding-horizon action selection, not an isolated tensor distortion. Holding the planner, candidate pool, rollout convention, tie rule, and all non-target sites in FP16 makes the one-site intervention interpretable; aggregating its ranking influence into a memory-constrained assignment connects a diagnostic to deployment. The design therefore keeps the backbone and planner fixed, tests the allocation signal against local-reconstruction allocation, and stays separate from LeFlow's planner redesign and QuantWAMs' joint video/action denoising.

plain_method_steps_zh.what_to_do: 输入 FP16 action-conditioned latent world model、planner inputs、candidate pool，以及 quantization site/bit-pair candidates。固定 planner inputs、candidate action-sequence pool、receding-horizon convention、tie rule 和 latent rollout evaluator。每次只暴露一个可量化的 weight/activation site，其余 sites 保持 FP16。输出是一个可复现的 frozen probe；它对同一批 candidate sequences 返回 FP16 和 one-site-quantized rollout scores。
plain_method_steps_zh.why_this_makes_sense: 这样可以在 action-conditioned latent-dynamics branch 中隔离 site-level perturbation，也能避免把 planner redesign 或 WAM denoising changes 误认为 quantization effects。

plain_method_steps_zh.what_to_do: 输入来自 S1 的 frozen probe outputs。对每个 site 和 bit pair，比较 FP16 与 one-site-quantized candidate ordering 在 imagined latent rollouts 上的变化，并保留按 horizon 区分的 influence values I_g(b)。输出是 site-by-bit influence profile I_g(b)；它按 rollout horizon 和 quantizable site 建立索引。
plain_method_steps_zh.why_this_makes_sense: ranking estimand 把 tensor reconstruction error 与 planner 的 decision-level sensitivity 连接起来，也包含 selected action 改变后产生的下游后果。

plain_method_steps_zh.what_to_do: 输入 site-by-bit influence profile、candidate bit pairs、backend-specific byte accounting、target bit histogram 和 memory budget B。为每个 site 选择 weight/activation bit pair，使 aggregate influence 在 measured `PeakBytes` 和 fixed nominal bit histogram 约束下最小。输出是 mixed W/A assignment `b*` 和 quantized checkpoint candidate。
plain_method_steps_zh.why_this_makes_sense: 这样可以把 diagnostic profile 转成 deployable mixed W/A PTQ assignment，同时不改变 latent planner，也不把 measured memory 换成 nominal byte assumption。

plain_method_steps_zh.what_to_do: 输入 quantized checkpoint candidate，以及 S1 中保持不变的 planner 和 evaluation convention。把 assignment 应用到 frozen planner，运行它原本的 imagined action-sequence 和 receding-horizon loop。在规定的 horizon conditions 下记录 candidate-order agreement、first-action agreement 和 closed-loop task success。在这个既有的 all-sites evaluation 中，把 representative high/low-influence site pairs 作为 tactical interaction diagnostic：在相同 candidate pool、bit histogram、measured `PeakBytes`、memory target、planner schedule、receding-horizon convention 和 tie rule 下，比较 measured joint candidate-order discordance 与对应的 single-site values。如果无法构造 exact feasible match，就记录该 diagnostic unavailable；任何 discrepancy 只用于限定 site-wise allocation interpretation，不定义新的 estimand，也不声称 joint optimality。输出是 closed-loop rollout outcomes 和 decision-level diagnostics，用来判断 RankCal 的 allocation signal 是否具有 load-bearing 作用。
plain_method_steps_zh.why_this_makes_sense: 需要保留的对象是 selected action 及其后续 consequences，因此 evaluation 留在 latent-dynamics planning 中，不切换到 joint video/action denoising。这个 pair diagnostic 在同一个 all-sites evaluation 内测试 interaction boundary，不改变 site-only estimand 或 falsification prediction。
